decision: New Organizational Setup for API Management
rationale: New organizational setup with dedicated testing repository eliminates the need for dynamic API key switching, resolving AUDIT-007.
Implement a dedicated 'docs' branch for synchronized README and UML updates to ensure documentation accurately reflects current implementation and usage.
Ratified that the current Usage section in README.md is sufficient for manual testing after user review.
Postpone explicit checklist database/caching implementation until Phase 2 to focus on core retrieval and parsing.
Adopt asynchronous, parallel requests for individual checklist generation instead of batching to ensure reliability, auditability, and context limit compliance.
Adopt SQLAlchemy (SQLite) for metadata and AI logging, paired with a local file system for binaries. Governance data is explicitly excluded from this DB to maintain a decoupled, reusable system.

Adopt Team G's recommendation for total decoupling via Protocols/Interfaces and Adapters. This ensures the core engine remains framework-agnostic and provides maximum long-term scalability for Django or other UIs.

Adopt Segmented Matching for task paths. The system will split the path by '/', attempting an exact literal match for each segment before falling back to normalized (fuzzy) matching. This preserves hierarchy and minimizes false positives.
Adopt 'urllib.parse' for standard-compliant, case-sensitive hierarchical path resolution. This ensures scalability for future web integration and avoids platform-specific path issues.
Modify `Settings.load()` to accept an optional dictionary of environment variables, allowing settings to be loaded from arbitrary sources without affecting the global environment.

Adopt semantic navigation for task resolution. Instead of complex string parsing, the system will leverage GitHub's 'tree' vs 'blob' metadata to find directories matching task segments, ensuring accurate leaf-level targeting and preventing accidental full-level downloads.
Adopt 'pydantic-settings' (BaseSettings) to ensure standard prioritization where execution flags and initialization arguments strictly override environment variables and .env files.

Implement AI analysis caching using a composite key of the instruction PDF hash and the system prompt hash. This prevents redundant Gemini API calls while ensuring results are automatically refreshed if the AI logic is updated.
Moved task ID resolution from an `explore` method parameter to a `GitHubStrategy` constructor parameter (`resolve_task_id`).
Implemented heuristic filtering to prioritize instructions matching task identity and exclude "AdditionalReading" documents to improve AI analysis quality.
Refactored Settings into logical mixins (GitHub, AI, System) using multiple inheritance and implemented `Unpack` for `get_settings` overrides.

Aligned hashing strategy between RepoStructure and RawSubmission to enable pre-fetch deduplication. Migrated AI checklist caching from memory to SQLAlchemy to prevent redundant analysis across sessions.
Adopted Python backend with SQL (SQLite3/MySQL) for structured relational data and Mongo for flexible document-based governance data to support multi-project isolation.

Adopted Team G's two-phase session: Phase 1 publishes agent rationales for public deliberation, Phase 2 gathers simultaneous blind votes. A secondary debate round is triggered if consensus threshold is not met.

Abandoned the SQL/Mongo hybrid model (DEC-064) in favor of a single local SQLite database per project. Used SQLite's native JSON support (JSON1) to store flexible governance documents (rationales, votes) alongside structured relational tables to ensure ACID compliance and zero external dependencies.

Adopted a high-level, paradigm-agnostic component diagram to outline module boundaries (CLI, Orchestrator, Voting Engine, Database Layer, Settings Config) and dependencies before starting the implementation.

Ratified SQLAlchemy ORM mapped models using SQLite JSON columns for flexible governance records. Implemented physical tenant isolation by routing connections to a project-specific database file located at .agents/governance.db.
Ratified formal auditing rules: audit logs are immutable, corrections require new re-audit entries, and generalized roadmap items must be split into granular, easily auditable sub-tasks.

Adopted the official google-genai SDK for AI queries. Built separate registry.py (to query active teams from SQLite) and prompter.py (to format paradigm-based system instructions and handle queries) modules, using mocks for offline unit testing.

Implemented the deliberation engine (Phase 1) using python's asyncio and the SDK's client.aio async client. This queries all active team agents concurrently, reducing API wait time from ~15-20s to ~2-3s.

decision: 5-Cycle Autonomous AI Voting with User Ratification
rationale: Ratified up to 5 rounds (cycles) of consensus voting where previous cycle rationales and tallies are fed back as context. Adopted Option 3: Only AI agents vote in the loop, and the final consensus is presented to the user for Approve/Reject ratification.

Ratified Option 1 (Layered Caching & Config-Driven Budgets) to prevent rapid API expense drainage. Deliberations and intermediate voting rounds are persistently cached. Config settings enforce max token caps and budget limits.
Ratified Option 1 (Migrate Roadmap to SQLite) to introduce a RoadmapTask table in the SQLite database, synchronized bidirectionally with .agents/roadmap.csv in migration.py.
